lead_headline: Claude Code's release-day triage sweeps fifty issues while new regressions surface in the connector stack
lead_body: A coordinated batch close around 22:35 resolved roughly fifty issues spanning the desktop app, CLI, hooks, MCP, and permissions — the shape of a release-day sweep rather than organic triage. Two substantive PRs landed: a credential-guard plugin and a word-boundary fix to the @claude trigger. Fresh reports of MCP servers not respawning after autoupdate and a broken Cowork spawn pipeline suggest the release introduced lifecycle regressions faster than they were caught.
lead_article:
Claude Code dominated the day, and the shape of that activity tells a story. A mass-close event around 22:35 swept out roughly fifty issues in a single batch — bugs across the desktop app, CLI, hooks subsystem, MCP integration, and permissions logic all marked resolved at once, which reads like a coordinated release-day triage rather than organic close-out. Against that backdrop, two PRs of substance landed: a credential-guard plugin for hardcoded secret detection, and a word-boundary fix to the @claude trigger that was misfiring on @claude-* bot names. The CLI-desktop conversation sync proposal also opened as a PR, which has been a long-standing gap in the multi-surface story.

The new issues surfacing after that batch close are worth watching. MCP stdio servers torn down during plugin autoupdate and not respawning is a quiet reliability hole, and the report that Cowork's MCP tool binding broke entirely after the 2026-05-23 auto-update — spawn pipeline missing --mcp-config — suggests the release may have introduced a regression in the connector stack. A separate thread on session-only crons silently missing scheduled fires during idle sessions points at the same territory: lifecycle management under the new plugin architecture is producing edge cases faster than they're being caught upstream. Astro shipped a single PR caching resolved actions in the base pipeline, a focused correctness fix. Hydrogen saw one issue filed against mutually exclusive deploy flags.
